report.headline: Projected to take a career-high 23.8% usage share in the EuroLeague, while the accompanying efficiency projection carries no real signal.

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 23.8% in the EuroLeague, up from 17.6% in the NBA source season, and above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.0%.

risks.text: Turnover rate was high at 21.0% in the source season, a real cost attached to the heavy playmaking role that is projected to grow further in the EuroLeague.

The true shooting projection of 56.0% should not be trusted: on this metric the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than simply guessing the EuroLeague average (4.3%), so the projection carries no information beyond that baseline.

The subject's source-season efficiency was already below the NBA average (51.5% true shooting, -0.53 sd), and only about half of a player's standing on this metric is estimated to carry across leagues (slope 0.532), adding further doubt to any efficiency improvement in the EuroLeague.

The cohort behind this estimate is players who sat only -0.31 sd below their own league's average when they made this move, and the estimate itself rests on 115 historical transitions, so it is a moderately sized but not deep sample to generalize from.

strengths.text: Assist rate of 28.7% and 7.033 assists per 75 possessions in the source season point to a playmaking role that the model expects to expand rather than shrink after the move, consistent with the projected usage rise to 23.8%.

The usage projection is built on a model that beats the trivial league-mean baseline (3.2% mean absolute error versus 4.2%), so the direction and rough magnitude of the usage increase can be trusted more than a coin flip.
Despite a below-average NBA usage rate (-0.50 sd), the fitted slope for usage carries over almost fully across this transition (0.977), which is consistent with the sizeable projected jump to 23.8%.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 19.4% to 28.2%, a span of 8.8 points against a league standard deviation of 4.5%, so the model can say this player projects above average but cannot pin down where in that range they land; the 95% interval widens further to 17.0%-30.5%.
